core_obligations: Construction (proof lines 6278-6300): in the case of exact countable direct sums the assertion is a consequence of the preceding discussion; in general the author forms the differential bigraded object A with F^{p+1}K^{p+1+q} in degree (p, q), observes that the inclusion alpha : (A, d) -> (A, d)[-1, 1] is an injective morphism of differential objects, and applies the self-map construction with S = [0, 1] and T = [1, -1].
Bidegrees (proof lines 6300-6306): because T^r S = [r, -r+1], the differential of the resulting spectral sequence is d_r : E_r^{p, q} -> E_r^{p+r, q-r+1}, which is the claimed bidegree.

The first two pages (proof lines 6308-6320): the author computes E_0 as a cokernel of alpha, obtains E_0^{p, q} = gr^p K^{p+q} with d_0^{p, q} = gr^p d^{p+q}, and then reads the descriptions of the boundaries and cocycles off the self-map remark, which yields E_1^{p, q} = H^{p+q}(gr^p(K)).
proof_roadmap: Dispose of the countable direct sum case by the preceding discussion.
Build the differential bigraded object whose inclusion is injective and apply the self-map construction.
Read off the bidegree of the differentials and identify the first two pages.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces the spectral sequence of a filtered complex of an abelian category, with differentials of bidegree (r, -r+1) and first pages the associated graded and its cohomology (statement lines 6265-6276). The proof is a complete argument: after noting that the countable-direct-sum case follows from the preceding discussion, the author constructs a differential bigraded object out of the filtration steps, shows that the natural inclusion is an injective morphism of differential objects, applies the abstract construction of a spectral sequence from such a morphism with the stated bidegree shift (proof lines 6278-6306), and then unwinds the definitions to identify E_0 and E_1 (proof lines 6308-6320). The non-formal content is the choice of the bigraded object and the unwinding of the abstract construction. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
